evidence: CONTEXT. I read the 'Inner child love' section as a first-time reader. It is one paragraph: the hand-on-heart and hand-on-solar-plexus practice with the words said to 'Little one', then 'Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death.', then the draft as the last sentence: 'If you can’t do this in a loving way today, just put your hands there and see what you feel, no faking required.' It follows from the sentence before it: that sentence sets a bar (really talking to a scared child, lovingly) and this one says what to do on a day you can’t meet it. Pronouns are fine: 'this' is the loving talking, or saying the words (the same 'in a loving way' as the instruction, and either parse gives the same practice), 'there' is the heart and solar plexus named earlier, and 'you' is the reader because the 'you' spoken to the child sits inside the quotation marks. It sounds like Joel (casual, as in 'scared to death' and 'just'). The apostrophe in can’t is the same curly one as the section’s don’t and I’m; there is no space before the full stop, no its/it’s slip and no quote marks around inner child. The draft appears once in CONTEXT.txt and matches DRAFT.txt exactly. SOURCE AND THE CHANGE. SOURCE.txt’s replaced words are 'If you can’t do this in a loving way today, just put your hands there and see what you feel. You don’t have to fake it!'. The draft keeps that first sentence word for word and turns the second into the tag ', no faking required', which is his own wording in his inner child guide as SOURCE.txt quotes it ('No warmth today? Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required.'). Every part of that guide line is carried (no warmth today, hands there, notice what is there, no faking) and nothing is added: no new claim, step or fact ('see what you feel' for the guide’s 'notice what you find' is the same instruction and is unchanged from the replaced words). It does not clash with the published text (don’t recite the words like an incantation the subconscious will grade; say them as to a frightened child you actually love): this is the fallback for a day without that warmth, and it lets go of pretending. It does what the_change says: it ends on 'no faking required', not on the linter-failing 'You don’t have to fake it!' and not on the rule-like 'Don’t fake it.' I could not see Emulate’s raw sample (batch 479, sample ch), so I judged the words as they stand against SOURCE.txt and the_change. TELL ROWS. I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the draft in its context and found none actually happening. The nearest calls: T10 and T22 (the tag is a permission in a calm, reassuring register) are not present, because it is not the 'you don’t have to X before Y' formula (no 'before Y', no requirement carried), it answers the exact pressure this paragraph has just built ('actually talking to your inner child', 'in a loving way'), it holds a stance (do not perform warmth, which sits with the published 'not an incantation' point) in a wry idiom, and it is his own wording; it also drops the second-person 'You don’t have to fake it!' sentence and its exclamation mark. T28, T20 and T29: in CONTEXT.txt the draft is the last sentence of the section (the writer’s ledger line for T28 says it is not the end of its section, which is not so for this context), so I checked it as the closer: it is the fallback itself, a new consideration the paragraph needs and the source has, ending on a plain three-word tag, not a lesson, healing line, summary, moral or quote-card line; without it the paragraph would have no fallback at all, so it does not complete a thought already complete. T26: 'in a loving way' recurs from the instruction two sentences earlier, and that callback is what lets 'this' point back, so the repetition has a job. T21 and T08: one condition and one action with a tag, not several argumentative jobs, and the tag does not explain the hands, it says what the fallback does not require. T14 and T15: the only swap is to his own words from his inner child guide, and nothing is moved or dropped. T13 and T09 (the rows D9 points to): the sentence notices that warmth can fail on a given day ('today') and swaps the demand to feel loving for 'see what you feel', and the weight is not equalised (the paragraph spends its force on 'scared to death'). T27: no tic words. C01 to C04: the draft does not name the inner child, the referents are clear, there is no invented first-person fact and no named-entity claim. LINTER. 'D9 follows the source order' (1/1 paragraphs, agreement 1.00): accepted. It is one paragraph with one fallback step, and the order (no warmth today, hands there, notice, no faking) is simply the order of what is being said (condition, action, release); nothing is reordered, moved or cut, and the sentence notices something (T13 and T09 above). 'E36/E41 heavy second person' (13.0 per 100): accepted. The 13.0 is 3 second-person words (you, your, you) in this 23-word sentence; the tag has none, and the replaced words had 4 in 26 (15.4), so the draft is lighter. The second person is the instruction to the reader of a practice card, as in every other sentence of the section, not a run of coaching lines.
